summary: Jack Kornfield is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dartmouth College, Saybrook University (PhD), and under Wing-tsit Chan, Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock Meditation Center.
Jack Laughlin is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at McMaster University in 1999 and held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jack Petranker is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as Research Director at the Yeshe De Project (attested 2004) and Director of the Mangalam Research Center for Buddhist Languages (attested 2012).
Jacob Antoon van Velze was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. in 1938 at Utrecht University, where he studied under Willem Caland and Jan Gonda.

Jacob Ensink was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Frederik David Kan Bosch. From 1954 to 1962, he served as Lecturer of Indology at the University of Groningen.

Jacob Fisher works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. A DPhil student at the University of Oxford (2021–2025), he has held posts at Nalanda Monastery, Wadham College, the University of Oxford, and Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Jacob Grimm was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Marburg (ca. 1802–1806). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (ca. 1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a Master of Arts under Kirill Solonin at Fo Guang University (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held positions as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Neusner was a religious studies scholar educated at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held posts at UW–Milwaukee, Brandeis, the University of South Florida, and as Distinguished Service Professor at Bard College (ca. 1994–2014).

Jacob P. Dalton, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Michigan. He held posts at the British Library, SOAS, Yale University, and became Distinguished University Professor at UC Berkeley and Dharmamitra.

Jacob Samuel Speyer was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Athenaeum and Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, he served as a professor at the University of Amsterdam, University of Groningen, and Leiden University.

Jacob Wackernagel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).
Jacobus Arntz was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He taught philosophy, philology, and natural sciences at Kuilenburg Seminary (1843–1847, 1862–1865) and at the Major Seminary of Roermond.
Jacobus Marinus van der Hoogt was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam in 1929 under the supervision of Barend Faddegon.

Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under William R. LaFleur at UCLA (MA 1990) and served as a professor at Princeton University from 1990 to 2019.

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned her doctorate under Julius Lipner. She has served as a faculty member and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Manchester.

Jacques André was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied under Jules Marouzeau at the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held posts at Aix-Marseille University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Paris Nanterre University.

Jacques Bacot was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot at the EPHE, where he later became directeur d’études, and served as President of the Société Asiatique from 1945 to 1954.

Jacques David Ehni was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his Dr.Theol. at the University of Tübingen. He held teaching posts at the Lyceum of Ludwigsburg and the Humboldt-Gymnasium Ulm.
